formMetadata.purpose: Form I-693, Report of Immigration Medical Examination and Vaccination Record, is completed jointly by an applicant for adjustment of status and a USCIS-designated civil surgeon to document the results of the required immigration medical examination and vaccination assessment under INA §212(a)(1) and 8 CFR §232.2.
formMetadata.situations: Required for all applicants filing Form I-485 (adjustment of status) except certain categories with overseas medical exams (refugees, derivative asylees under INA §209, K nonimmigrants who completed panel physician exams abroad). Also required for certain other immigration benefits requiring medical clearance. The medical examination covers communicable diseases of public health significance (TB, syphilis, gonorrhea, Hansen's disease), physical/mental disorders with associated harmful behavior, drug abuse/addiction, and required vaccinations per INA §212(a)(1)(A) and CDC Technical Instructions for Civil Surgeons.
formMetadata.use-cases: 1) I-485 applicant (family/employment-based) obtains sealed I-693 from civil surgeon to submit with adjustment package. 2) Refugee adjusting under INA §209(a) needs only vaccination assessment (Part 10), not full medical exam, if overseas exam was completed. 3) K-1 visa holder adjusting status needs vaccination-only assessment if panel physician exam was done abroad. 4) Applicant with positive TB screening requires chest X-ray and possibly sputum cultures before civil surgeon can sign. 5) Applicant requiring referral to health department for TB treatment — civil surgeon completes Part 8 Item 5 referral, health department completes Part 9. 6) Applicant with mental health condition requiring evaluation for harmful behavior assessment.
formMetadata.filing-context: I-693 is submitted with Form I-485 in a sealed envelope prepared by the civil surgeon. It may be submitted at filing or brought to the interview. The I-693 is valid for 2 years from the date the civil surgeon signs Part 7 (not the date of the examination). If submitted more than 60 days after the civil surgeon signs, USCIS may require a new exam. The applicant completes Parts 1-2 (and Part 3 if interpreter, Part 4 if preparer). The civil surgeon completes Parts 5-10. The applicant must NOT sign Part 2 until instructed by the civil surgeon. Edition 01/20/25; OMB expires 09/30/2027.
formMetadata.parties-involved: Applicant: The person seeking adjustment of status who undergoes the medical examination; completes Parts 1-2, provides personal and contact information. Civil Surgeon: A USCIS-designated physician who performs the immigration medical examination, completes Parts 5-10, and certifies findings; must have a valid Civil Surgeon Identification Number (CSID). Interpreter: Translates the form for the applicant if needed; completes Part 3. Preparer: Prepares Parts 1-2 on behalf of the applicant; completes Part 4. Evaluating Physician/Health Department: Completes Part 9 if a referral evaluation is required by the civil surgeon.

Part 2, Item 4. Applicant's Signature. Full certification: 'I certify, under penalty of perjury, that I provided or authorized all of the responses and information contained in and submitted with my application, I read and understand or, if interpreted to me in a language in which I am fluent by the interpreter listed in Part 3., understood, all of the responses and information contained in, and submitted with, my form, and that all of the responses and the information are complete, true, and correct. I understand the purpose of this immigration medical examination, and I authorize the required tests and procedures to be completed. If it is determined that I willfully misrepresented a material fact or provided false or altered information or documents with regard to my immigration medical examination, I understand that any immigration benefit I derived from this immigration medical examination may be revoked, that I may be removed from the United States, and that I may be subject to civil or criminal penalties. Furthermore, I authorize the release of any information from any and all of my records that USCIS may need to determine my eligibility for an immigration request and to other entities and persons where necessary for the administration and enforcement of U.S. immigration law.' CRITICAL TIMING: Form states 'NOTE: Do not sign or date Form I-693 until instructed to do so by the civil surgeon.'
fields.notes: Must be signed in the presence of the civil surgeon. Do NOT pre-sign. Missing signature invalidates the form.
